text.p: Swiss watchmaker Gerald Piaget, credited by experts with launching women's jewelled wristwatches after World War Two, has died, his family said on Monday.
Piaget, 79, worked with his father who set up the family business at Cote-aux-Fees, in Neuchatel canton, where production of expensive, prestige pieces continues.
He died at Areuse, in Neuchatel canton, on Saturday, according to the Swiss news agency ATS, which cited a family announcement but gave no cause.

"He was a great watchmaker who created the woman's jewelled watch bracelet that we know today. He launched it after the war," Osvaldo Patrizzi, a watch expert and chairman of Antiquorum Auctioneers in Geneva, told Reuters.
In 1988, Piaget was acquired by South African-controlled Richemont Securities, a Zug-based company which in turn owns 70 per cent of Vendome Luxury Group.
Vendome owns a number of watchmakers including Cartier, Baume-Mercier and Vacherin-Constantin.
